Reference: Set up

Reference for the "Set up" group of qargi commands: every verb with its arguments, options and examples, generated from the release.

Updated 2026-11-05

  • qargi methodology
  • qargi cloud

  • qargi role

qargi project #

Store the answers about a project, once, outside the repository.

The answers are the repository, its long-lived branches, the roles that exist (build, write, review, test) with each role's base branch, model, effort, packages and skills, the memory stores, the budget, and optionally a lead with teams and a push grant. Provisioning and dispatch read them. Push policy per role is none: an agent never pushes; the lead's grant is separate (qargi help push).

VerbWhat it does
templatePrint an answers file with defaults
initValidate and store an answers file
newStart a new project: its directory, a git repository on the methodology's branches and generic files
attachAttach to an existing repository: read it, show the answers and the gaps, store on approval
adoptAdopt an attached repository: create the missing long-lived branches and the missing methodology files on a branch to review
setChange one answer
showPrint the stored answers and what they mean
listList the stored projects
validateCheck an answers file without storing it (a WARN line for each pack linked to a role that is not in the pack library, and for a profile that still carries the shipped template header)
profileCheck the repository's profile: the shipped template header, and gate commands the repository does not know (check)
linkMake this work tree load the project's skills, agents and memory from ~/.qargi
unlinkUndo project link in this work tree and restore the backups

qargi project template #

qargi project template NAME

Print an answers file with defaults.

Edit it, then store it with init. models.provider is empty and must be set (the provider the project's agents run on; there is no default); project validate reports it while it is not. No role names a model: it takes the provider's tier once one is set.

qargi project init #

qargi project init NAME [OPTIONS]

Validate and store an answers file.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--answersFILEthe answers file to store
--forcereplace stored answers
qargi project template acme > acme.json
qargi project init acme --answers acme.json

qargi project new #

qargi project new NAME [OPTIONS]

Start a new project: its directory, a git repository on the methodology's branches and generic files.

Prints the plan (directory, branches, files, deployment options with instructions) and a token; with --plan and --approved it creates the directory, runs git init, writes the generic files in a first commit and creates the long-lived branches. Nothing is pushed and no remote is created: say where it goes with git. The files mention no tool of yours. They include an AGENTS.md with a Development environment section and a Makefile with stub bootstrap and doctor targets (the doctor fails until you fill it in); see qargi help environment.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--methodologyNAMEthe methodology (default gitflow)
--dirDIRwhere to create it (default ./NAME; must be absent or empty)
--paramNAME=VALUEa methodology parameter as name=value (repeat), for example test_command
--urlURLthe repository URL; with it the qargi answers are stored too
--deploymentIDa deployment option to record and explain (see qargi methodology deployment)
--providerNAMEthe provider the project's agents run on (models.provider, with its models); not stored when omitted (qargi provider list)
--provider-localNAMEthe runtime of the local surface (models.provider.local); use it with --provider-cloud instead of --provider
--provider-cloudNAMEthe runtime of the cloud surface (models.provider.cloud)
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log
qargi project new acme --param test_command='make test'
qargi project new acme --dir ~/src/acme --url https://github.com/me/acme

qargi project attach #

qargi project attach [DIR] [OPTIONS]

Attach to an existing repository: read it, show the answers and the gaps, store on approval.

Reads the repository (branches, tags, version and changelog files, test command, CI) and changes nothing in it. Prints the answers it would store, the gaps against the methodology and what it could not determine, and a plan token. With --plan and --approved it stores the answers outside the repository. The safe gaps are closed by qargi project adopt, the rest by hand. It reads the tree of the methodology's integration branch (develop), else of the default branch, else of HEAD, and says which; never the working tree. It prints origin as read and the https url it normalises to. If answers are already stored it shows stored against detected, lists the fields the stored file lacks, stays read-only and gives no plan token; with --force the plan replaces what it detects and keeps what it cannot (the roles' models and effort, cloud, memory, budget). It reports what it found of the development environment (section, task runner, bootstrap and doctor commands) and lists the pieces that are missing as gaps. It never guesses a provider: models.provider (and the roles' models) are stored only with --provider NAME, and without it the output says so; with --force --provider fills in a provider that is not set and never replaces one.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--nameNAMEthe project name (default: from the remote or the directory)
--methodologyNAMEthe methodology to compare with (default gitflow)
--urlURLthe repository URL, when it has no origin remote
--providerNAMEthe provider the project's agents run on (models.provider, with its models); not stored when omitted (qargi provider list)
--provider-localNAMEthe runtime of the local surface (models.provider.local); use it with --provider-cloud instead of --provider
--provider-cloudNAMEthe runtime of the cloud surface (models.provider.cloud)
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log
--forcereplace the detected answers, keep the rest

qargi project adopt #

qargi project adopt [NAME] [OPTIONS]

Adopt an attached repository: create the missing long-lived branches and the missing methodology files on a branch to review.

Prints the plan and a token: the local branches it would create (at the default branch tip; main stands for master; none is moved) and the files from the methodology that do not exist, written as one commit on agent/adopt-NAME cut from develop. With --plan and --approved it creates exactly that. Existing branches and files are never changed, nothing is pushed or checked out, and a second run finds nothing to do. Changelog format, tag format and CI content are listed as left for you, and so are the bootstrap and doctor targets a repository with a task runner lacks (an existing file is not edited). The AGENTS.md section it drafts names the repository's own runner. Refused (exit 2) with a dirty working tree, a detached HEAD, no commits, a project that is not attached, and in a member run.

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--methodologyNAMEthe methodology (default: the project's, else gitflow)
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log
qargi project adopt acme
qargi project adopt acme --plan TOKEN --approved "go ahead"

qargi project set #

qargi project set [NAME] PATH VALUE

Change one answer.

PATH is dotted (budget_cents, roles.write.effort, lead.push); VALUE is JSON or a plain string. models.extensions and models.accept_no_barrier are refused here: they change only through qargi provider enable|disable and qargi provider accept. roles.ROLE.tools is the list of the tools a role needs beyond its apt packages, each {kind, name, ...}: kind go (name a package path, version a tag: go install NAME@VERSION), kind binary (name the file name, version, url of the file itself, sha256 of it: downloaded to ~/.local/bin and kept only when the hash matches) and kind submodule (name as in .gitmodules, path: checked out in each member clone by qargi local prepare). env plan lists them, env apply installs them and env check reports one that is missing or wrong; a member's guard refuses setting them (and a whole role), as it refuses release.*, test_command, env.* and site.*.

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

qargi project set acme roles.write.effort high
qargi project set acme packs.none true
qargi project set acme roles.test.tools '[{"kind":"go","name":"acme.test/ci","version":"v1.2.0"}]'

qargi project show #

qargi project show [NAME]

Print the stored answers and what they mean.

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

qargi project list #

qargi project list

List the stored projects.

qargi project validate #

qargi project validate FILE

Check an answers file without storing it (a WARN line for each pack linked to a role that is not in the pack library, and for a profile that still carries the shipped template header).

qargi project profile #

qargi project profile SUBCOMMAND [NAME] [OPTIONS]

Check the repository's profile: the shipped template header, and gate commands the repository does not know (check).

Read only, so a member may run it. check reads the profile (the gates, rules and review steps of a repository, outside the repository) and prints FAIL for each line at the top that is still the shipped example's (the Example profile title and the Copy to line of examples/myproject/profile.md), exit 1; and WARN for each backticked command in its Gates section that is found in none of the repository's instruction files and Makefile targets (a make target of the Makefile, the command's text in one of the three files, or a script that exists), exit 0. No profile is fine (said, exit 0); a --profile file that is not there is exit 2. Without NAME the project is the one in effect, else the repository of the current directory. project validate prints the header finding as a WARN line.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--profileFILEthe profile file to read (default: ~/.qargi/config/profiles/<repository>.md, the repository being the project's directory name)
qargi project profile check acme
qargi project profile check --profile ./profile.md

qargi project link #

qargi project link [PROJECT] [OPTIONS]

Make this work tree load the project's skills, agents and memory from ~/.qargi.

One plan and one token for every resource, each placed and linked the way the project's runtime says (a directory link, one link per entry, or a copy). A real directory in the way is moved to NAME.qargi-backup, never deleted. Run it inside a work tree to link that one; nothing records which work trees exist. A member's guard refuses it.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--resourceLISTwhat to link: skills, agents, memory (comma separated; default every one the runtime links and that exists)
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log

qargi project unlink #

qargi project unlink [PROJECT] [OPTIONS]

Undo project link in this work tree and restore the backups.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--resourceLISTwhat to link: skills, agents, memory (comma separated; default every one the runtime links and that exists)
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log

qargi methodology #

List and inspect the development and release methodologies.

A methodology is the way a project is developed and released, as data: its branches, versioning and changelog, test tiers, CI, release steps and deployment options, and the generic files a new project starts with. One ships with qargi (gitflow); add your own under ~/.qargi/config/methodologies/NAME/ (methodology.json and a scaffold/ directory). These verbs only read; qargi project new and adopt write, and only after a plan.

VerbWhat it does
listList the methodologies and where they live
showPrint a methodology: branches, tests, CI, release steps, parameters, scaffold, deployment options
checkValidate one methodology, or all of them
filesPrint the scaffold rendered with the parameters, writing nothing
deploymentList the deployment options, or print one option's instructions

qargi methodology list #

qargi methodology list

List the methodologies and where they live.

qargi methodology show #

qargi methodology show NAME

Print a methodology: branches, tests, CI, release steps, parameters, scaffold, deployment options.

qargi methodology check #

qargi methodology check [NAME]

Validate one methodology, or all of them.

qargi methodology files #

qargi methodology files NAME [OPTIONS]

Print the scaffold rendered with the parameters, writing nothing.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--paramNAME=VALUEa parameter as name=value (repeat)
qargi methodology files gitflow --param project=acme --param test_command='make test'

qargi methodology deployment #

qargi methodology deployment NAME [ID]

List the deployment options, or print one option's instructions.

qargi cloud #

Which ant profile and workspace each project uses.

A project can be bound to an ant profile and the workspace that profile must reach (the project's optional cloud answer). Every qargi command about that project then runs ant under that profile, and a cloud call is refused if the profile no longer reaches the workspace, so work never lands in another project's workspace. A project without a binding uses ant's active profile. qargi stores and checks the binding; it never reads or writes a token. login runs ant auth login on your terminal; a member or a script cannot.

VerbWhat it does
listPrint every project's binding
showPrint one project's binding
setBind a project to an ant profile and a workspace
unsetRemove a project's binding
checkCheck that the profile exists and reaches the workspace (reads the ant profile only)
loginLog the project's profile in, bound to its workspace (your terminal only)

qargi cloud list #

qargi cloud list

Print every project's binding.

qargi cloud show #

qargi cloud show [PROJECT]

Print one project's binding.

qargi cloud set #

qargi cloud set [PROJECT] [OPTIONS]

Bind a project to an ant profile and a workspace.

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--profileNAMEthe ant profile name
--workspace-idIDthe workspace the profile must reach (wrkspc_...)

qargi cloud unset #

qargi cloud unset [PROJECT]

Remove a project's binding.

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

qargi cloud check #

qargi cloud check [PROJECT]

Check that the profile exists and reaches the workspace (reads the ant profile only).

qargi cloud login #

qargi cloud login [PROJECT]

Log the project's profile in, bound to its workspace (your terminal only).

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

qargi agent #

Name the members: the local agents that do the work.

A member is a local agent you name, rendered from the one member definition qargi ships, with the roles it serves: build, write, review, test (all four by default). The render is kept in the configuration directory (agents/PROJECT/NAME.EXT beside agents.json, outside every repository) and written from there to the runtime's agents location; a checkout cleaned or cloned afresh gets it back with agent refresh. The task block names the role and carries its role text (roles/<role>/ROLE.md); there is no skill to load. Review is read-only as a rule: the guard refuses changes to the clone under that role. Under every role it refuses the verbs that change a skill (qargi skill|tool new, import, seal, remove, link, unlink, enable, disable; qargi discover install; qargi packs apply) and writes in the pack library, the credentials directory and install.json, ~/.claude/skills and any .claude/skills directory; it fails closed. Dispatch spawns the member qargi agent for ROLE prints.

VerbWhat it does
addCreate a member under a name you choose
listList the members of every project, their roles and definitions
renameRename a member and its definition
refreshRe-render a member from the member definition qargi ships now
modelsShow the base members, the profiles with their resolved models and efforts, and each member
removeDelete a member's definition and its record
forPrint how to dispatch a role: the base member, the model alias and the effort

qargi agent add #

qargi agent add NAME [OPTIONS]

Create a member under a name you choose.

A member belongs to a project, and the definition is rendered by the provider of that project. Refuses a name that exists, a name that is not kebab-case, the name of a built-in agent type of that provider, no --project (exit 2), and a project with no provider (exit 2: there is no default provider). Nothing is written to a runtime's user-level directory.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--rolesLISTcomma-separated roles it serves (default build,write,review,test)
--modelMODELmodel alias or id for the definition (default: the project's model for the first role, else the shipped default; see agent models)
--effortLEVELeffort level, written into the definition and recorded with the member (default as for --model)
--projectPROJECTthe project the member belongs to (required): its models.provider renders it, the render is kept in the configuration directory (agents/PROJECT/) and the runtime's file goes where the runtime links project agents (the checkout, hidden from git, or the project render once `project link` is applied)
qargi agent add forge --roles build,test --project myproject
qargi agent add scribe --roles write --model opus --project myproject
qargi agent add worker --project myproject    # the write-class base: build, write and test

qargi agent list #

qargi agent list [OPTIONS]

List the members of every project, their roles and definitions.

One row per member, with no header line: PROJECT, NAME, ROLES (comma separated), MODEL/EFFORT, FILE, then in brackets MISSING (the runtime's file is gone), STALE (the copy in the configuration directory is gone or changed, or the definition, catalog, renderer or an extension changed since the render) or DRIFT (the file was edited by hand), each followed by the command that fixes it: qargi agent refresh NAME --project P. Members are kept per project, so two projects can each have a worker.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTonly the members of this project

qargi agent rename #

qargi agent rename OLD NEW [OPTIONS]

Rename a member and its definition.

Within its project. The project is --project, else the one in effect, else the only project that has a member OLD; a name two or more projects hold, with none named or in effect, is refused (exit 2) and lists them.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project the member belongs to (default: the one in effect when it has the member, else the only project that has it)

qargi agent refresh #

qargi agent refresh NAME [OPTIONS]

Re-render a member from the member definition qargi ships now.

The project is found as for rename. Keeps its name, roles and model, and writes the copy in the configuration directory and the runtime's file again: a file that is gone (a cleaned checkout, a fresh clone) comes back, a file edited by hand is replaced (the output says so). Use it after an upgrade changes the definition (for example its hook); an unchanged member is left alone. Sessions started afterwards use the new definition.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project the member belongs to (default: the one in effect when it has the member, else the only project that has it)

qargi agent models #

qargi agent models [OPTIONS]

Show the base members, the profiles with their resolved models and efforts, and each member.

Two base members, one per guard class: worker (build, write, test; may write) and reviewer (review; read-only). Everything else is a profile {base, tier, effort, purpose} resolved at dispatch: the shipped ones are in lib/model-defaults.json (build, write, test, review, auditor, advisor, researcher, lead), a project adds or overrides its own under profiles.NAME in its answers, and a provider file (lib/providers/NAME.json; the project's models.provider) maps the tiers fast, balanced, deep and frontier to models. The frontier tier (researcher) is opt-in. Problems are flagged on their row, never fatal: a member that is not a base (nothing dispatches it), a missing base, a refused project profile, a mixed-class member, a tier with no alias, a frontier member outside researcher. A project is needed, because its models.provider decides the models: --project, else the one in effect (with none, exit 2). The members shown are that project's (`agent list` shows all projects'). Read-only.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project, instead of the one inferred from here
--jsonmachine-readable

qargi agent remove #

qargi agent remove NAME [OPTIONS]

Delete a member's definition and its record.

The project is found as for rename: --project, else the one in effect, else the only project that has the member; a name in two or more projects with none named is refused (exit 2).

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project the member belongs to (default: the one in effect when it has the member, else the only project that has it)

qargi agent for #

qargi agent for ROLE [OPTIONS]

Print how to dispatch a role: the base member, the model alias and the effort.

The base member is the one the profile names (worker for build, write and test, reviewer for review) when the project has registered it; no other member serves, and without it the verb says which base to add. A read-only role never resolves to a member that can write. Plain output is one line: MEMBER MODEL EFFORT PROFILE; pass MODEL and EFFORT to the Agent tool with the member as subagent_type.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project whose members serve and whose profiles apply (default: the project of the current directory)
--profileNAMEa profile of the role's class (a shipped one such as auditor, advisor or researcher, or the project's own; default: the role's own)
--surfaceSURFACElocal (default) or cloud: with cloud, resolve the registered base instance (<project>-worker or -reviewer) instead of a member; needs --project
--opt-incloud only: confirm an opt-in profile such as researcher
--jsonmachine-readable: role, class, profile, base, member, tier, model alias, model id, effort (cloud: instance, base, model, effort, profile, class)

qargi role #

List and check the roles: what a member or cloud agent is for.

A role is a directory with role.json (its class, write or read-only, and a description) and ROLE.md (its instructions). Four ship with qargi: build, write, review and test (review is read-only). Add your own under ~/.qargi/config/roles/NAME/: a name of one lower-case token, never lead. The class decides what the guard allows a member (read-only: nothing in the clone changes); the text of a role cannot change it. A task block carries the role's text; a cloud agent of the role has it in its system prompt.

VerbWhat it does
listList the roles, their class and where they live
showPrint a role: its class, description and instructions
promptPrint a role's instructions as a task block carries them
checkValidate one role, or all of them

qargi role list #

qargi role list

List the roles, their class and where they live.

qargi role show #

qargi role show NAME

Print a role: its class, description and instructions.

qargi role prompt #

qargi role prompt NAME

Print a role's instructions as a task block carries them.

qargi role check #

qargi role check [NAME]

Validate one role, or all of them.

qargi provider #

List and check the model providers: tiers, models and what each can do.

A provider is a descriptor, lib/providers/NAME.json, with one schema for every provider: the model each tier (fast, balanced, deep, frontier) maps to, with the date and source it was verified, the effort levels it understands, the one surface it serves (local or cloud) and a capability matrix for it: model and effort overrides at dispatch, a fixed tool list per agent, a read-only barrier, a session budget ceiling, memory stores, skills and MCP. A capability that is not verified counts as not supported. A provider with no read-only barrier on its surface cannot serve the review role there unless you accept that with qargi provider accept. The project's models.provider chooses the provider; there is no default, and a verb that needs one refuses a project with none (exit 2). A family name (what several runtimes of one vendor share) stands for the runtime of a surface only in a project's models.provider and in provider of; every verb that takes a NAME (show, check, model, addenda, adapter-run, effective, require-barrier, layout, launch, require-skills) takes a runtime name, and a family name is refused as an unknown provider.

VerbWhat it does
listList the providers with the surface each serves and whether the descriptor is clean
showPrint one provider: tiers and models, effort levels and its capability matrix
acceptRecord that you accept a provider surface that has no read-only barrier
checkValidate a definition (a library name or a directory) and say what degrades
newScaffold a provider, catalog or extension pack in the library
importImport a provider pack from a directory, a JSON file or an https git URL, after a review
sealRecord the current content of a library provider pack as approved
removeRemove a library provider pack
enableLet a project use a library extension pack
disableStop a project using a library extension pack
adapter-runRun one verb of a runtime's adapter (a library pack's adapter runs only as a sealed private copy, removed afterwards)
addendaPrint the texts a runtime's definition adds to the member contract (a cloud agent's prompt, or the run's contract directory on the local surface)
notesPrint a note of the project's runtime (local unless --surface cloud), or list the topics it has
modelPrint the model a runtime maps a tier to on a surface
attestRecord a capability you verified by hand or by a paid run (never runs or spends anything itself)

qargi provider list #

qargi provider list

List the providers with the surface each serves and whether the descriptor is clean.

qargi provider show #

qargi provider show NAME [OPTIONS]

Print one provider: tiers and models, effort levels and its capability matrix.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--jsonmachine-readable
--projectPROJECTshow it as this project sees it, with its verified extensions composed in

qargi provider accept #

qargi provider accept NAME [OPTIONS]

Record that you accept a provider surface that has no read-only barrier.

Without --plan and --approved it prints what would be recorded and a plan token. Applied, it writes models.accept_no_barrier.SURFACE (who, when, why) to the project's answers and the audit log. It is the only way a provider surface whose read-only barrier is not supported can serve the review role.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--surfaceSURFACEthe surface the acceptance covers
--no-barrieraccept running the review role without a read-only barrier on that surface
--projectPROJECTthe project whose answers record it (default: the project of the current directory)
--askedWORDSyour words asking for it
--approvedWORDSyour words approving the plan
--planTOKENthe plan token printed without it

qargi provider check #

qargi provider check NAME|DIR [OPTIONS]

Validate a definition (a library name or a directory) and say what degrades.

Fails on a definition that breaks the schema, a name that differs from its file, a missing tier or an unknown capability. Warns on a verified date that is missing and says which capabilities count as not supported because of it, and which roles therefore cannot be served (for example review where the read-only barrier is not supported).

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTcheck it as this project composes it with its enabled extensions

qargi provider new #

qargi provider new NAME [OPTIONS]

Scaffold a provider, catalog or extension pack in the library.

Plan, token, approval, as for a skill. The pack is stored unsealed and counts for nothing until sealed.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--kindKINDprovider, catalog or extension
--fromNAMEstart from this provider's definition
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log

qargi provider import #

qargi provider import SOURCE [OPTIONS]

Import a provider pack from a directory, a JSON file or an https git URL, after a review.

The review lists files, executables (with hash and interpreter), URLs, network commands and secret findings. Binaries, archives, symlinks and secrets are refused; opaque blobs are flagged. A pack with executables also needs --approve-exec naming each. Stored sealed, never enabled; a shipped or existing name is refused.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--nameNAMEstore it under this name
--refREFthe git ref to pin
--pathSUBa subdirectory of the source
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log
--approve-execNAMESname every executable the pack holds, separated by commas, to approve running them

qargi provider seal #

qargi provider seal NAME [OPTIONS]

Record the current content of a library provider pack as approved.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved

qargi env #

What a repository declares about its development environment.

qargi defines no file for this. A project declares its environment with a section of AGENTS.md (or README.md) headed Development environment, Environment or Setup, the version pins in the standard files, and two runnable targets: bootstrap (install or update, idempotent) and doctor (check only). qargi reads them; see qargi help environment.

VerbWhat it does
showPrint what was found (section, pins, submodules, runner, targets) and the commands in effect
checkRun the project's doctor, add the qargi layer (links, members, packs, memory) and print ENV OK or ENV INCOMPLETE
planRun the dry run of the bootstrap, show it grouped by privilege, print a plan token (the lead's; runs project code)
applyRun the bootstrap command once, for a plan you showed (the lead's)

qargi env show #

qargi env show [OPTIONS]

Print what was found (section, pins, submodules, runner, targets) and the commands in effect.

Read-only, and a member may run it. Nothing is executed: make, just, task and mise are never run, their files are read as text (at most 1 MB each; a symbolic link that leaves the repository is refused). The commands are derived from the targets (make bootstrap, make -n bootstrap, make doctor) and replaced by the project's answers env.doctor_command, env.bootstrap_command and env.dry_run_command; env.known_failures lists doctor lines accepted on this host. Each line says where it came from.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project, instead of the one inferred from here
--repoDIRthe repository directory (default: the project's repo.path, else the repository around here)
--jsonprint the result as JSON
qargi env show
qargi env show --project acme --json
qargi project set acme env.doctor_command 'make doctor'

qargi env check #

qargi env check [OPTIONS]

Run the project's doctor, add the qargi layer (links, members, packs, memory) and print ENV OK or ENV INCOMPLETE.

A member may run it. It RUNS THE PROJECT'S CODE: the doctor command (env.doctor_command, else the doctor or check target) is run once, without a shell, in the repository, with standard input closed and a minimal environment, so the repository is as trusted as it is for test_command. Its lines are read: one that begins with missing, fail, error, not ok, stale, [x] or a cross mark, or ends with missing, not found or not installed, is a missing item; one that begins with expected or contains an env.known_failures entry is expected and not red; a non-zero exit with no such line is one missing item. With no doctor command a built-in minimum runs: submodules initialised, tags present when the repository has a remote and releases, and every tool a pin file names found on PATH, answering --version and matching the pin's major.minor (this runs TOOL --version). For a stored project it then checks the tools the roles declare (roles.ROLE.tools): a go tool or a binary that is not installed, is another version (go version -m) or another file (sha256) or sits in a directory PATH lacks, and a declared submodule that is not initialised or at another commit, are missing items. It adds, read-only, whether the checkout loads the project's skills, agents and memory, whether the members are current (STALE, DRIFT), packs check and memory check. The last line is ENV OK or ENV INCOMPLETE: N missing (...); exit status 0, 1 or 2 (usage, no such project, no repository). The verdict, HEAD, time and commands are recorded under check in state/env/PROJECT.json (mode 600, the other keys are kept); no command output is.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project, instead of the one inferred from here
--repoDIRthe repository directory (default: the project's repo.path, else the repository around here)
--timeoutSECONDSseconds the doctor may run (default 300, at most 3600)
--jsonprint the result as JSON
qargi env check
qargi env check --project acme --timeout 60
qargi env check --repo ~/src/acme --json

qargi env plan #

qargi env plan [OPTIONS]

Run the dry run of the bootstrap, show it grouped by privilege, print a plan token (the lead's; runs project code).

A dry run is not harmless: make -n still expands $(shell ...) and runs recipe lines marked + or holding $(MAKE), and the dry run of the other runners evaluates project code too. So the plan itself runs project code, and needs --approve-exec naming the executable; read the project's files first. The command runs without a shell, in the repository, with standard input from /dev/null, a minimal environment (PATH with absolute entries, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, LANG, LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, TERM, TZ, TMPDIR) and a limit of QARGI_ENV_TIMEOUT seconds (default 120). Its output is shown line by line, the privileged lines (a command in the line is sudo, doas, pkexec, su or run0) apart from the others, then the executables seen in the lines. Lines and executables are read from the text, best effort: a recipe can run more than its dry run shows. Then the tools the roles declare (roles.ROLE.tools), each with its state here (ok, missing, wrong, path: in a directory PATH lacks); apply installs the go tools and binaries that are missing or wrong, so the token line names go in --approve-exec when a go tool is among them. The plan token is a hash over the output, the commands, the tools, the repository and its HEAD, and the host name. A member's guard refuses it.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project, instead of the one inferred from here
--repoDIRthe repository directory (default: the project's repo.path, else the repository around here)
--approve-execNAMEthe executable of the dry-run command (make for make -n bootstrap); without it nothing is run and the exit status is 2
qargi env plan --approve-exec make
qargi env plan --project acme --approve-exec make

qargi env apply #

qargi env apply [OPTIONS]

Run the bootstrap command once, for a plan you showed (the lead's).

Runs the dry run again (project code, as plan does) and refuses when its token is not --plan, when --approve-exec does not name the two executables, and when the plan has privileged lines and --allow-root is not given. Then the bootstrap command runs once, without a shell, with the minimal environment of plan and with standard input, output and error inherited, so sudo can ask on your terminal: run it in a terminal you are at. No password is read or kept. Apply writes two lines to the audit log (start and result, with your words), then installs the declared tools the plan showed as missing or wrong: go install NAME@VERSION for a go tool, and for a binary the file at its URL, downloaded to a temporary name, kept only when its sha256 is the declared one, made executable and moved to ~/.local/bin/NAME (a failed tool is named, the others still run, exit 1). It records the run in ~/.qargi/state/env/NAME.json (mode 600) and then runs qargi env check (the project's doctor), whose verdict ends the output and whose exit status is the verb's. QARGI_DRY_RUN stops it after the checks, before the bootstrap runs. A member's guard refuses it.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--projectPROJECTthe project, instead of the one inferred from here
--repoDIRthe repository directory (default: the project's repo.path, else the repository around here)
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log
--approve-execNAMESname the executables of the dry-run and the bootstrap commands, and go when the plan installs a go tool, separated by commas (others the plan listed may be added)
--allow-rootallow a plan that has privileged lines (sudo, doas, ...)
qargi env apply --plan 0123456789ab --approved "install the tools" --approve-exec make,go
qargi env apply --plan 0123456789ab --approved "go" --approve-exec make,pacman --allow-root

qargi packs apply #

qargi packs apply INSTANCE|PROJECT [OPTIONS]

Update an existing cloud agent, or render for a local runtime.

Without --target (or with managed-agents) this updates the existing cloud agent INSTANCE with its skills and tools; the lead's GitHub tool arrives this way when the project grants a cloud push. It needs --asked, and always needs --plan (QARGI_NESTED does not skip it); a local member's guard refuses it. With --target claude-code it takes PROJECT instead of INSTANCE and needs no --asked. Without --approved it prints a plan token. With --plan and --approved it renders the project's enabled skills and tools into $QARGI_STATE/render/PROJECT/RUNTIME (claude-code for this target), replacing the previous render atomically, and prints the exact `claude --add-dir ...` launch line (with --mcp-config and --settings when the render has them). A local runtime cannot enforce role scoping, so the render is the union of the project's roles and role scoping is advisory there. Skills render under .claude/skills; tool packs render mcp.json and settings.json. Nothing is written into a repository or into ~/.claude, and members cannot write under the state's render/ directory. The plan refuses, naming the pack and writing nothing, a skill whose SKILL.md name differs from the pack name, whose front matter is not closed or has more than one name key; a skill and a tool with the same name; and a tool allowlist name outside letters, digits, _, . and -. Each plan stages into its own hidden directory and a lock serializes concurrent applies; the second refuses if the render changed meanwhile. The swap installs only the tree the token approved; the token also covers the file modes, which the manifest records.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--targetTARGETclaude-code renders for a local session; managed-agents (the default for apply) is the cloud update
--askedREQUESTthe request, in your words, that names the cloud instance; recorded in the audit log
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log

qargi packs seed #

qargi packs seed [OPTIONS]

Add or update the baseline packs shipped with qargi in your library.

qargi ships a few packs (packs/ in its tree). Seeding stores them in your library. Without --approved it prints one line per pack (add, update, current or kept) and a plan token. A pack you edited and sealed, or one of your own with the same name, is kept and never overwritten; an untouched shipped copy is updated when qargi ships a newer text. Seeding never links a pack: nothing reaches a project or an agent until you link it.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--installonly add the packs the library lacks, without a token (install.sh --user runs this)
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log

qargi packs check #

qargi packs check [PROJECT] [OPTIONS]

Check a render for drift (read only).

Needs --target claude-code. Writes nothing and exits 1 on any finding: library drift (a pack changed or failed review since it was rendered), rendered tampering (a file differs from the manifest, or an extra or missing file), enablement drift (a pack enabled or disabled, or its roles changed, since the render), shadowing of a rendered skill by ~/.claude/skills or by the checkout's .claude/skills, and a render directory that has no manifest (a broken render). A project with no render at all is not a failure: the check prints a not applied line with the command that applies it and exits 0. The answer packs.none: true says the project uses no project packs; the check then passes with no render, and fails if a pack is linked to a role of the project. It also reports a rendered file that differs from the library copy (even when the manifest was edited with it), a changed file mode, a group- or world-writable render, a malformed manifest, and a manifest that names another project or whose role scoping is not advisory. It ends with a section, skills a session would load, that gives every skill a session opened in the checkout would load one state: qargi (a library pack with approved content, or a skill shipped with qargi), accepted (skill accept), drifted (accepted, but its content changed: this exits 1), excluded (switched off in the provider's settings; qargi only reads them) or unmanaged (everything else, shown with what to do about it; this does not change the exit status). When the checkout's skills directory is not linked to the render it adds a note naming packs link.

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--targetTARGETclaude-code renders for a local session; managed-agents (the default for apply) is the cloud update

qargi packs link #

qargi packs link [PROJECT] [OPTIONS]

Make the project's checkout load its packs by itself.

The provider's project skills directory in the repository (for Claude Code .claude/skills) becomes a symbolic link to the render made by packs apply --target. Without --approved it prints the plan, the skills a session would load, and a plan token; apply with --plan TOKEN --approved. If the directory is absent it creates the link; if it is already that link it says so and exits 0. It refuses a link to anywhere else, a symlinked parent, a checkout that is not the top of a git work tree, a missing render, and files tracked by git. If it is a real directory the plan lists each skill in it as same, differs or new against the library and offers skill import and skill link for the new ones; apply then moves the directory to the backup name (skills.qargi-backup beside it) and links, so skills not imported stop loading until they are. Nothing is deleted. If git does not ignore the path it prints the line to add to .git/info/exclude and never edits that file. A provider that has no such directory is refused (exit 3). Every verb that takes --target (packs apply, packs check), packs link and unlink, skill accept and marshal handoff exit 2 when the project has no provider (qargi project set P models.provider NAME). A local member's guard refuses it.

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log

qargi packs unlink #

qargi packs unlink [PROJECT] [OPTIONS]

Undo packs link.

Removes only the symbolic link that points to this project's render and, if the backup exists, moves it back to the skills directory. Refuses a link to anywhere else, a real directory in its place, and a backup with no link of ours. Same plan token and approval as link; nothing else is deleted.

PROJECT can be left out inside the project's repository, or set QARGI_PROJECT.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--planTOKENthe plan token printed by the same command without --approved
--approvedWORDSyour go-ahead for exactly that plan, in your words; recorded in the audit log

qargi discover #

Find, recommend and install tools for the roles of a project.

A tool is a skill, an MCP server, a package for the sandbox or a built-in tool of the agent. search looks in the reviewed catalog and your library and, with --online, in the official MCP registry and Anthropic's skills. recommend ranks the catalog for each role of a project by the stack it sees in the repository, leaving out what the role has. install asks which scope the tool should reach (user, user-role, project, project-role), then goes through the existing gates: a skill or an MCP server is imported with its review and your approval of exactly that content, linked at the scope, and offered to the cloud agents it reaches with the plan shown first. Nothing found online is installed on trust. install changes skills, so a local member's guard refuses it.

VerbWhat it does
sourcesList what is searched
searchSearch the catalog, your library and, with --online, the registries
recommendRank the catalog for the roles of a project
showShow one entry: what it is, its risk and how it installs
installInstall an entry: review, approval, scope, link

qargi discover sources #

qargi discover sources

List what is searched.

qargi discover search #

qargi discover search QUERY [OPTIONS]

Search the catalog, your library and, with --online, the registries.

OptionArgumentWhat it does
--kindKINDonly this kind: skill, mcp, package or agent-tool
--roleROLEonly tools recommended for this role
--onlinealso search the MCP registry and Anthropic's skills
qargi discover search pdf
qargi discover search github --online --kind mcp

qargi discover recommend #

qargi discover recommend [PROJECT] [OPTIONS]

Rank the catalog for the roles of a project.

OptionArgumentWhat it does

qargi discover recommend acme --role build
